div.head: Northu 1
div.ab: Gyf hwa ænigum preoste ænig woh beode, beon ealle geferan mid biscopes filste georne ymbe þa bote ⁊ beon to ælcan rihte, swa swa hit awriten is, quasi cor unum et anima una.
Gyf hwa ænigum preoste ænig woh beode, beon ealle geferan—mid biscopes filste—georne ymbe þa bote and beon to ælcan rihte, swa swa hit awriten is, quasi cor unum et anima una.

Wenn jemand irgend einem Priester irgend ein Unrecht anthut, seien alle Genossen [des Domstifts] mit des Bischofs Hilfe eifrig bemüht um [Erlangung der] Busse und seien zu jeder Rechtssache [des Einzelnen], wie es geschrieben steht, ‘wie ein Herz und eine Seele’.

If anyone does any wrong to any priest, let all the fellows [of the chapter], with the bishop's help, be eager about [obtaining] compensation, and let them be at every legal matter [of an individual], as it is written, ‘as one heart and one soul’.

If anyone offer wrong to any priest, all his colleagues are to be zealous about obtaining the compensation with the help of the bishop, and in every matter of law they are to be, just as it is written, “as if one heart and one soul”.

If anyone inflicts harm on any priest, all of his fellows—with the bishop’s help—are to be persistent about the compensation, and in every legal matter they are to be, just as it is written, as one heart and one soul.
div.note: Some of Liebermann’s notes here are cut off in the gutter of the scan used, and are still to be completed.

Liebermann compares Acts 4.32 and the Canons of Edgar.; U: checked against Whitelock, EHD I (1979), and corrected (before: ‘If anyone offer wrong to any priest, all his colleagues are to be zealous about obtaining the compensation with the help of the bishop, and in every matter of law, they are to be, just as it is written, "as if one heart and one soul".’).; AU: corrected against Rabin p. 302 / 303, October 2026 (was “Gyf hwa ænigum preoste ænig woh beode, beon ealle geferan—mid biscopes filste—georne ymbe þa bote and beon to ælcan rihte, swa swa hit awriten is, quasi cor unum et anima una.”, now “Gyf hwa ænigum preoste ænig woh beode, beon ealle geferan—mid biscopes filste—georne ymbe þa bote and beon to ælcan rihte, swa swa hit awriten is, quasi cor unum et anima una. (expanded letters in italics: quasi cor unum et anima una)”); W: corrected against Rabin p. 303, October 2026 (was “fellows— with”, now “fellows—with”)
one heart and one soul: Acts 4:32.

note.seg: Die Geistlichen beon anræde quasi cor unum; Polity ed. Thorpe 432, ebenso soll der Bischof auf der Synode klagen und bei den Genossen (Mitbischöfen) Unterstützung zur Abhilfe finden; 428
The clergy are to beon anræde quasi cor unum; Polity ed. Thorpe 432; in the same way the bishop is to make complaint at the synod and find support for redress among his fellows (fellow bishops); 428
Nicht alle Mitpriester allgemein oder auch nur des ganzen Sprengels, sondern die Kathedralgilde, die laut 2, 1 bestimmt geschlossen ist und laut 2, 2 eigene Kasse besitzt
Not all fellow priests in general, or even those of the whole diocese, but the cathedral guild, which according to 2, 1 is a definitely closed body and according to 2, 2 has its own funds
Vermutlich als Zeugen und Eideshelfer bei Klageeid wie Reinigung; s. u. 31f.; vgl. Gl Genossenschaft 3 ff.
Presumably as witnesses and oath-helpers, in the oath of accusation as well as in exculpation; see below 31f.; cf. Gl Genossenschaft 3 ff.
